Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors: 
  - Severe "blinding" headache for 3 days, onset on waking; persistent, partially responsive to ibuprofen (pain rated ~8/10 reducing to ~5/10).  
  - Pain generalized, worse over right eye. Photophobia and intermittent "shooting lights" / visual phenomena. Nausea without vomiting. Occasional stabbing pain when standing or moving head. No fever, no cough, no sinus symptoms.  
  - Uses combined oral contraceptive pill (started ~1 year ago) — noted as a thrombotic risk factor by DDx.  
  - Functional impact: difficulty working, missed one full day and partial work inability.  
- Relevant family medical history: 
  - Mother with severe migraines (with vomiting). Patient reports no other family medical history.  
- Medications (including OTC or shared medications): 
  - Combined oral contraceptive pill — dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  - Ibuprofen (taken intermittently for headache) — dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  - Paracetamol recommended by clinician to take concurrently — dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  - Clinician stated intention to prescribe a stronger analgesic (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).  
- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.  
- Sexual and reproductive health: 
  - On combined oral contraceptive pill ~1 year. Pharmacy BP checked when pill issued ~1 year ago and reported normal per patient.  
  - Clinician advised that if migraine with aura is confirmed, the pill may need review/change. No pregnancy test or STI history recorded.  
- Physical activity and nutrition: Not recorded.  
- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use: 
  - Non-smoker.  
  - Drinks alcohol: patient stated "probably like, three, once a week" (quantity/frequency ambiguous).  
  - No recreational drug use reported.  
- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded.  
- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk): 
  - Reports some lack of energy, attributed to the persistent headache. No other mood disorder symptoms, depression, or self-harm risk documented.  
- Vision problems or recent changes: 
  - Photophobia and intermittent visual phenomena ("shooting lights").  
  - Patient reports a recent eye check with "nothing changed" in vision.  
- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Key findings and impressions (transcript + DDx consistent): 
  - Young woman with new severe persistent headache for 3 days with photophobia and visual phenomena; partial response to analgesia; family history of migraine. Clinician considers migraine but recommended in-person neurological exam and fundoscopy to exclude secondary causes.  
  - DDx highlights primary migraine as the leading diagnosis but also raises medium-likelihood secondary causes given OCP use (CVST, IIH) and low-likelihood SAH.  
- Relevant differential diagnoses (from DDx and consistent with transcript): 
  - Probable migraine with visual aura — high likelihood (fits photophobia, visual phenomena, family history, partial analgesic response).  
  - Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) — moderate likelihood (young woman on combined OCP with subacute progressive headache and visual symptoms); requires exclusion.  
  - Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) — moderate likelihood (young woman with persistent headache and transient visual disturbances); requires fundoscopy and further assessment.  
- Working diagnosis and management priorities: 
  - Working diagnosis: Probable migraine with visual phenomena (probable aura).  
  - Management priorities: perform a full neurological examination and fundoscopy (face-to-face), measure blood pressure, reassess suitability of combined OCP if migraine with aura is confirmed, and exclude secondary causes (CVST, IIH, SAH) with clinical assessment and urgent imaging if indicated. Advise ED attendance if headache becomes unbearable, changes, or neurological signs develop.

Management Plan

- Key management actions, treatments, and recommendations provided: 
  - Arrange face-to-face appointment via support team for full neurological examination and fundoscopy (booked by patient if she chooses).  
  - Clinician to prescribe a stronger analgesic (name unspecified) — patient advised to take with food. Paracetamol was recommended to be taken concurrently. (Prescription name/dose/route/frequency not documented.)  
  - Continue combined oral contraceptive pill for the moment; clinician to check BP and review pill suitability at in-person visit — change may be required if migraine with aura is confirmed.  
  - Safety advice: go to Emergency Department (A&E) if headache becomes unbearable, worsens, changes in character, or if new neurological symptoms occur. Contact the clinic for further advice if concerns arise.  
- Follow-up and referrals: 
  - In-person review planned for examination; no specialist referral arranged in the transcript. Specialist referral may be considered after examination depending on findings.  
- DDx-supported reasoning reflected in management: 
  - Because DDx includes CVST, IIH and (less likely) SAH, clinician prioritized urgent clinical examination (neurological exam and fundoscopy) and safety netting for urgent imaging/ED review if examination or symptoms suggest secondary cause.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Migraine (probable migraine with visual aura) — High likelihood.  
  - Justification: Photophobia and subjective visual phenomena ("shooting lights"), severe pain interfering with function, partial response to ibuprofen, family history of migraine, no fever or focal neurological deficits on history.  
- Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) — Moderate likelihood.  
  - Justification: Young woman on combined oral contraceptive pill (increased thrombotic risk), subacute progressive severe headache with visual symptoms; positional/stabbing element reported. Requires exclusion with clinical exam and imaging if indicated.  
- Idiopathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) — Moderate likelihood.  
  - Justification: Young woman with persistent headache and transient visual disturbances; fundoscopy required to assess for papilledema. Lack of obesity and lack of other typical features do not exclude IIH.
